lines: Everything on this slab came out from under somebody kitchen floor this morning.
No boats, no nets, no going anywhere. You open the hatch and you wait.
Cut, dried, bundled, graded. Thatching, screening, and the long stuff.
The long stuff has to be nine feet clear and there are maybe two beds that give it.
One of them is on the far side of the broken span, which is why it costs what it costs.
Glowcaps, two to a jar, lids loose so they can breathe.
They last a week. People buy them anyway, every week, for eighty years.
It is not a lamp. Nobody has ever bought one thinking it was a lamp.
If you drop money through the boards it is gone. Actually gone.
There is a man who dives for it in the summer. He is not poor.
